spots.name: Giardino degli Aranci (Parco Savello)
spots.blurb: A walled garden of orange trees on the Aventine hill that ends at a stone balustrade over the Tiber, with the dome of St Peter's lined up in the middle of the view. Locals bring a book to the benches under the trees; the crowd thickens only in the last half hour before sunset.
spots.tips: Go before 9am for an empty terrace, or arrive 45 minutes before sunset and claim a bench on the left side of the belvedere. The keyhole of the Knights of Malta is 100 m away and usually has a queue.

safety.note: Gated park that closes at dusk; busy and well-frequented at sunset.

spots.verifyNote: Existence and free access confirmed via search. Only it.wikipedia surfaced for the name, so the English title was set to null rather than guessed.

spots.name: Villa Doria Pamphili
spots.blurb: Rome's biggest landscaped park: umbrella pines, a formal parterre below the Casino del Bel Respiro, a small lake and long grassy slopes where Monteverde residents jog, nap and picnic. It is large enough that even on a Sunday you can find a stretch of lawn with nobody in earshot.
spots.tips: Enter from Porta San Pancrazio (Via di San Pancrazio) or Via Vitellia; the meadow south of the lake gets the last sun of the day. Bring water; cafe options inside are limited.

safety.note: Gated park, closes at dusk; plenty of runners and dog walkers throughout the day.

spots.verifyNote: Not searched (budget). Well-known public park; Wikipedia title from reviewer knowledge.

spots.name: Villa Celimontana
spots.blurb: A small hilltop park five minutes from the Colosseum that most visitors walk straight past: gravel paths, an Egyptian obelisk, palms and a view towards the Baths of Caracalla from the back edge. Nannies, retirees and students share the grass, and the benches under the trees stay shaded all afternoon.
spots.tips: Enter from Piazza della Navicella. The lawn on the southern side is the quiet one; the playground end fills up around 5pm on school days.

safety.note: Gated park that closes at dusk.

spots.verifyNote: Not searched (budget). Well-known public park; Wikipedia title from reviewer knowledge.

spots.name: Villa Sciarra
spots.blurb: A hillside garden on the Monteverde flank of the Gianicolo with 18th-century statues, a mossy fountain of satyrs and terraces of wisteria that bloom in April. It is one of the emptier green spaces near the centre because it has no famous view and no cafe.
spots.tips: Enter from Via Calandrelli; the upper terrace benches catch the afternoon sun. Wisteria peaks in mid-April, which is the one week it gets busy.

safety.note: Gated park, closes at dusk; residential surroundings.

spots.verifyNote: Not searched (budget). Public municipal park; Wikipedia title from reviewer knowledge.

spots.name: Parco degli Acquedotti
spots.blurb: A wide open plain on the south-east edge of the city where a line of Roman aqueduct arches runs to the horizon, crossed by dog walkers, runners and the occasional flock of sheep. There are no gates and no shops, only long grass and the arches, so sunrise here feels like being outside the city altogether.
spots.tips: Metro A to Giulio Agricola or Subaugusta, then a 10-minute walk. Bring a blanket and water; the park is unlit after dark, so leave by dusk or go in a group.

safety.note: Unlit and isolated after dark; enjoy it from dawn to dusk, or go with friends at night.

spots.verifyNote: Not searched (budget). Well-known public park within the Appian Way regional park; Wikipedia title from reviewer knowledge.

spots.name: Orto Botanico di Roma
spots.blurb: The university's botanical garden climbs the lower slope of the Gianicolo behind Palazzo Corsini: a bamboo grove, a Japanese garden with a pond, greenhouses and a hillside of oaks where you hear almost nothing from Trastevere below. The small entry fee keeps it near-empty on weekdays.
spots.tips: Bring a book to the benches in the Japanese garden; the bamboo grove is the coolest spot in summer. Last entry is an hour before closing.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Orto Botanico dell'Università di Roma "La Sapienza"

sources.title: Roma Capitale: L'Orto botanico, un'oasi di pace e verde a Trastevere

safety.note: Ticketed, staffed garden with daytime hours only.

spots.name: Non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico)
spots.blurb: A walled garden cemetery beside the Pyramid of Cestius, where cypresses, roses and a colony of cats shade the graves of Keats, Shelley and Gramsci. It is quiet in the way churches are, and visitors sit on the benches near Keats's grave and read for an hour.
spots.tips: Entry is by donation, requested at the gate. Keats's grave is in the old section by the pyramid; the cats gather there in the late afternoon. Keep voices low; it is a working cemetery.
spots.hours: Mon-Sat 9am-5pm, Sun 9am-1pm (last entry 30 min before; check site)

safety.note: Staffed, walled site with daytime hours.

spots.verifyNote: Not searched (budget). Long-established public site; Wikipedia title from reviewer knowledge.

spots.name: Biblioteca Angelica
spots.blurb: Rome's oldest public library, opened in 1604, is a two-storey wooden reading room behind the church of Sant'Agostino, a minute from Piazza Navona and silent enough to hear pages turn. Anyone with photo ID can register for free and read or work at the long tables under the vault.
spots.tips: Register at the front desk with a photo ID; bags go in the lockers. It stays cool in summer and some tables have power sockets.
spots.hours: Mon-Fri from 8:30am; closes early afternoon Mon/Fri, evening Tue-Thu (check site)

safety.note: Staffed state library in the busy centre.

spots.verifyNote: Not searched (budget). State public library; Wikipedia title from reviewer knowledge.

spots.name: Chiostro del Bramante (upper loggia cafe)
spots.blurb: Bramante's Renaissance cloister beside Santa Maria della Pace houses an exhibition space with a cafe on the upper loggia, where you can sit at a table in the arcade and look down into the courtyard. The cafe has generally been reachable without an exhibition ticket, and the noise of Piazza Navona disappears once you are inside.
spots.tips: Take the stairs up to the first-floor loggia; the cafe corner over the cloister has the best light. Weekday afternoons are the calmest. Ask at the desk if ticket-free access to the cafe is in effect that day.
spots.hours: Roughly 10am-8pm (cafe); varies with exhibitions, check site

sources.title: Chiostro del Bramante: Renaissance Architecture in Rome - ArcheoRoma

safety.note: Staffed venue in the historic centre.

spots.verifyNote: English Wikipedia URL confirmed via search; Wikipedia notes the venue includes a cafe and bookshop. Ticket-free cafe access softened to 'generally'.

spots.name: Giufà Libreria Caffè
spots.blurb: An independent bookshop-cafe in San Lorenzo, open since 2005, with tables between the shelves, a strong graphic-novel section and a back room where students sit with laptops. Nobody rushes you; one coffee buys you an afternoon.
spots.tips: Weekday afternoons are the quietest; evenings often host readings and book launches, so check the events page if you want silence. Wifi and a few sockets in the back room.

safety.note: Busy student district; streets around Piazza dei Sanniti are populated until late.

spots.verifyNote: Confirmed open at Via degli Aurunci 38. Draft hours ('until 1am') and the after-10pm tip were wrong: published hours are Mon-Sat 9am-10pm, Sun 3pm-9pm. Name corrected to the venue's own form.

spots.name: Tram Depot
spots.blurb: An outdoor kiosk built around an old tram carriage at the river end of Via Marmorata, with mismatched tables under trees and plants and Testaccio traffic filtered out by hedges. Locals come for a specialty coffee in the morning or a spritz in the evening and stay for hours.
spots.tips: Seasonal: it operates roughly from spring to autumn and closes in winter. Seating is all outdoors. It gets sociable after 9pm; late afternoon is the quiet window.
spots.hours: Seasonal (roughly spring-autumn), morning to late evening; check social pages

safety.note: Lit, staffed kiosk on a main street; populated until closing.

spots.name: Rinascente rooftop terrace (Via del Tritone)
spots.blurb: The top floor of the Rinascente department store on Via del Tritone is an open terrace with a panorama of domes from the Vittoriano to St Peter's, free to walk onto without buying anything. It is partly covered, with a bar if you want it and railings to lean on if you don't.
spots.tips: Take the escalators to the top floor; sunset is the prime hour and the busiest. Weekday mornings right at opening are nearly empty.

safety.note: Inside a staffed department store; open only during store hours.

spots.verifyNote: Not searched (budget). The Tritone store's free public rooftop is well documented since its 2017 opening; 'La Rinascente' Wikipedia article is about the company, so title left null.

spots.name: Isola Tiberina lower embankment
spots.blurb: The lower quay around Tiber Island, reached by steps from Ponte Cestio or Ponte Fabricio, puts you at water level with the weir's rapids a few metres away and the city a storey above. In summer the Lungo il Tevere stalls line the bank; the rest of the year it is just people sitting on the travertine with a drink or a book.
spots.tips: Sit on the downstream tip of the island for the loudest water. In summer evenings it is lit and busy; in winter go before dark. The quay can be closed when the river is high.

safety.note: Well-frequented and lit on summer evenings; quieter and dimmer in winter, so leave the lower quay before late night and stay off it when the river is high.

spots.verifyNote: Not searched (budget). Public embankment; 'Tiber Island' article is about this island, title from reviewer knowledge.

spots.name: Belvedere dello Zodiaco (Monte Mario)
spots.blurb: The terrace at the top of Monte Mario, the highest hill in the city, looks over the whole of Rome from the Vatican to the Alban Hills, and at night the view becomes a field of lights with the floodlit dome in the middle. It is a long-standing Roman spot for couples and quiet late-night drives, with a public balustrade and a bar next door if you want a table.
spots.tips: Bus up Via Trionfale or a taxi to Viale del Parco Mellini; the balustrade is free, the bar is not. The road up through the nature reserve is dark at night, so go with a friend late on.

safety.note: Terrace is lit and usually populated, but the access road through the park is dark; go with a friend after 11pm and avoid walking up alone.

spots.verifyNote: Not searched (budget). Well-known public belvedere on Viale del Parco Mellini; coordinates nudged to the terrace, medium confidence. 'Monte Mario' Wikipedia article is about the hill, not this terrace, so title left null.
